tip: When the question word is the subject, the verb comes right after it: 'vem har' = who has.
Reported questions use 'om' (if/whether) for yes/no questions: 'frågade om' = asked if.
'Vänta sig' means to expect, not just wait: 'hade inte väntat mig det' = hadn't expected it.
Particle verbs put the stress on the particle: 'rullar in' (rolls in), where 'in' adds the direction into.
Use 'i' before a month name to mean in that month: 'i juni' means in June.
Add '-s' to a verb for the passive: 'serverar' (serves) becomes 'serveras' (is served), no doer needed.
'Kvart' means a quarter hour in clock talk: 'kvart över nio' is a quarter past nine.
After 'kan' (can), the next verb stays in its base form, no 'att': 'kan du rekommendera' = can you recommend.
After 'att', 'inte' sits before the verb: 'att du inte kunde komma'. English doesn't move 'not' like this.
'På' plus a time span tells how long something took: 'på bara tre dagar' = in just three days.
With an adjective, 'the' appears twice, as 'den'/'det' plus the noun ending: 'den goda middagen', 'det fina sällskapet'.
Swedish normally drops the article for jobs after 'är': 'Han är lärare', not 'han är en lärare'.
For food that tastes good, use 'god' rather than 'bra': 'Smörgåsen är god' means the sandwich is tasty.
'Semester' means vacation, not a school term: 'Jag behöver semester' = I need time off.
'Somna' = fall asleep (the moment); 'sova' = to sleep (the state): 'vi somnade sent'.
Days of the week stay lowercase in Swedish, so 'söndag' is written small in mid-sentence.
'Ha råd' is the set phrase for affording something: 'har inte råd' = can't afford it.
Before an en-word, no is 'ingen': 'ingen aning'. Ett-words take 'inget', plurals take 'inga'.
'Än' means than after a comparative like 'bättre': 'bättre sent än aldrig' = better late than never.
'Varsin' means one each: 'Vi tar varsin fika' = we each get our own fika.
'Bra' never changes form for gender, number, or definiteness: 'en bra fråga', 'det är bra'.
'Lägga märke till' is the fixed phrase for to notice: 'lade märke till' = noticed.
When 'kort sagt' opens the sentence, the verb 'fungerar' comes before the subject 'det'.
Allergic to is 'allergisk mot', using 'mot' rather than 'till' or 'för': 'allergisk mot nötter'.
'Gott' is the '-t' form of 'god' because it describes the verb 'doftar', not a noun: 'doftar gott'.
'Checka in' = check in; the 'in' goes after the verb as its own word: 'vi checkade in'.
The '-s' on 'ses' means each other: 'vi ses' = we see each other, the usual way to say see you.
'Se' is irregular in the past: 'se' becomes 'såg' = saw, as in 'vi såg en fin film'.
'Så fort' literally means so fast but works as as soon as: 'så fort jag kan' = as soon as I can.
'Tycka om' means to like; 'om' is stressed and belongs to the verb: 'vi tyckte om maten'.
